The University of California, Office of the President, is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position. Salary offers are determined based on final candidate qualifications and experience. The full salary range shows the growth potential for this position and the pay scale is the budgeted salary or hourly range that the University reasonably expects to pay for this position.
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training

Minimum 10 years progressively responsible experience in labor relations, workforce compliance, policy/program management, or a closely related field, including substantive experience with collective bargaining, contracting out/covered services, or workforce compliance.
Minimum 4 years’ experience in a large, complex, decentralized organization.
$180,000.00 to $200,000.00, Commensurate with Experience

The WCO Associate Director, Workforce Compliance, Policy & Programs serves as the Director's second-in-command and senior operational, policy, and compliance lead for the Workforce Commitment Office. The position applies substantial labor relations and Article 5 knowledge to lead program execution, develop and maintain systemwide guidance, coordinate implementation across UC locations, and provide senior consultation on covered services, contracting, settlements, arbitration decisions, and related workforce compliance obligations. The Associate Director translates WCO strategy into sustainable programs, workplans, procedures, training, and implementation plans; owns major workstreams; builds consensus among internal and external stakeholders; and provides delegated Director coverage. The position exercises functional and project leadership without formal supervisory responsibility.

30% Leads execution of assigned WCO compliance programs and deliverables, including Qualified Individual (QI) reporting, Wage-Benefit Parity (WBP) Supplier Compliance Verification, Annual Article 5 Report workstreams, Covered Services initiatives, supplier compliance activities, and implementation of settlements, arbitration decisions, and related contracting out and reporting obligations. Tracks milestones and deliverables, identifies operational barriers and risks, and recommends corrective action to the Director as needed.

25% Provides senior operational policy and contracting out expertise; develops, maintains, and updates systemwide operational guidance, procedures, training, and compliance resources within established WCO policy direction. Interprets collective bargaining requirements, covered services provisions, settlements, arbitration decisions, and applicable laws and policies for implementation; identifies emerging issues and escalates novel, precedent-setting, or high-risk matters to the Director.

20% Coordinates systemwide consultation and implementation support with UC locations, Labor Relations, Procurement, OGC, suppliers, union representatives, and other stakeholders. Facilitates cross-functional meetings, coordinates routine communications and implementation activities, builds consensus, and provides practical guidance on complex workforce and contracting matters within delegated authority.

15% Operationalizes established WCO strategy and Director direction through implementation plans, workplans, RASC/RACI frameworks, milestones, standardized procedures, and monitoring approaches. Leads assigned cross-functional initiatives and process improvements that strengthen consistency, efficiency, compliance, and long-term sustainability, and reports progress, barriers, and recommendations to the Director.

10% Serves as second-in-command and deputy to the WCO Director as delegated. Provides delegated Director coverage, owns major operational workstreams, coordinates functional/project work across the Policy Analyst and Business Systems Analyst portfolios without formal supervision, tracks deliverables, identifies barriers, and escalates matters requiring Director-level strategic, executive, precedent-setting, or high-risk decisions.
Familiarity with Vendor Management Systems, Smartsheet, or similar enterprise workflow, reporting, or compliance systems.
25% Travel to UC locations and other systemwide meetings as needed for stakeholder engagement, implementation of WCO programs, and coordination of workforce compliance initiatives.
Labor Relations Representative 5
Benefits: For information on the comprehensive benefits package offered by the University visit: Benefits of Belonging
Advanced knowledge of labor relations, collective bargaining, contract and reporting requirements, contracting out/covered services, and related workforce compliance obligations.
Strong understanding of systemwide, campus, and/or medical center policies and procedures and the ability to assess how assigned work affects multiple areas across the system.
Advanced knowledge of policy and program implementation, process development, and methods for translating established requirements into practical and sustainable operational guidance.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to assess complex situations, identify operational risks, develop options, and make sound recommendations within delegated authority.
Working knowledge of legal, contractual, and policy requirements relevant to workforce contracting and compliance, with the ability to identify issues requiring escalation.
Ability to operationalize systemwide labor, procurement, workforce compliance, and related policies and processes within established direction and delegated authority.
Highly developed skills in stakeholder engagement, consensus building, facilitation, and cross-functional collaboration in complex or rapidly changing environments.
Highly developed written, verbal, and presentation skills for communicating complex information to all locations, suppliers, union representatives, Location partners, and leaders at varying levels.
Ability to lead major workstreams, exercise delegated authority, and provide functional/project leadership without formal supervisory responsibility.

Ability to develop and maintain operational guidance, procedures, training materials, and implementation resources, and to use data, reporting, and technology tools to support compliance oversight and improve program effectiveness.
